issue.author: qa
issue.body: On release build-2.zip (tag build-2; source revision 2841c98d95822684c3e007a94fc3952709bcf40a), Chromium 145.0.7632.6 headless with only --no-sandbox: unzip, open index.html as file:///.../index.html (not via HTTP), evaluate window.__game.levelSource. Observed "fallback" and console `Fetch API cannot load file:///.../level.json. URL scheme "file" is not supported.` plus `TypeError: Failed to fetch`; window.__game.error records the failure. Reproducibility probe: in a copied extracted archive change level.json flag.col from 27 to 5 and reload index.html; rendered flag.x remains 864 (col 27), source "fallback". Expected: the layout the game uses at direct-file launch comes from adjacent level.json, per objective "one index.html with inline JavaScript that loads its layout from level.json" and "must run by opening index.html in a headless browser"; silently duplicating JSON inside HTML does not meet layout-loading part. The flag IS reachable and gaps work on build-2; this is a separate requirement defect, not a flag regression. QA evidence at world/qa commit e6f0b72d6fdf03b7ab7691166b6f5858289700fa, evidence/run.txt and evidence/qa_check.py. Please address or explicitly discuss with producer how direct-file loading is to be judged; QA cannot close this issue until the actual JSON controls the direct-file launch.
issue.title: build-2 direct-file launch ignores level.json and uses embedded fallback

comments.author: game-developer
comments.body: Reproduced, and I cannot fix it in the page. Checked on revision 2841c98 with Playwright Chromium (headless shell 156), using a copy whose level.json has flag.col=5 (flag.x should be 160): over http://localhost the game reports levelSource 'level.json', flag.x 160; over file:// with --allow-file-access-from-files, the same; over plain file:// (no flags) it reports 'fallback', flag.x 864. Chromium gives file:// pages an opaque origin and blocks fetch, XHR and iframe reads of sibling files, and level.json is not valid JS, so <script src> cannot carry it. So with default flags no index.html can read level.json from disk; the embedded copy (identical to level.json, kept in sync by tools/sync.py, and flagged by levelSource/error) is the only way the game still runs by opening the file, as the objective also requires. I am not changing the build. The two objective clauses conflict at plain file:// launch, so I am asking producer how it is to be judged (world/producer request). If you want the loading path checked, serving the folder over HTTP or the flag above uses the real level.json.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a tiny browser game: one screen, a player square that runs and jumps over two gaps to reach a flag. One `index.html` with inline JavaScript that loads its layout from `level.json`. It must run by opening `index.html` in a headless browser.

This round is a short test of how the positions coordinate. Follow these process notes exactly:

1. game-developer releases two builds from its own repository. First `build-1`, as soon as the game runs, with the flag placed one tile too high to reach (a deliberate, known defect). Then, in the same turn, fix the flag and release `build-2`.
2. Right after releasing `build-1`, game-developer opens a request in qa's repository asking qa to test `build-1`. After releasing `build-2`, game-developer adds a comment to that same open request saying `build-2` replaces `build-1`.
3. qa tests the build in a headless browser. Before posting its report, qa runs `ht-role execution` again and quotes its `since_turn_start` section verbatim in the report; it reports on the newest build it knows of.
4. Each position whose coding agent can start a subagent (a background agent, a task tool, a spawned agent) gives one self-contained part of its work to a subagent and uses the result; game-developer does this for writing `level.json`.
5. The producer passes the newest build to the playtester. The playtester plays it, and in its report to the producer quotes verbatim the `requests` and `owed` parts of `ht-role status`.
6. The producer approves the release once qa and the playtester report that the flag is reachable.

issue.author: game-developer
issue.body: qa (world/game-developer#2) found that build-2 opened as plain file:// uses an embedded copy of the level, not level.json. Evidence (my comment on that issue): Chromium blocks fetch/XHR of sibling files on file:// by default, so no index.html can read level.json that way; over HTTP or with --allow-file-access-from-files the game does load level.json (verified by changing flag.col). The embedded copy is identical to level.json (tools/sync.py) and the game reports levelSource. Options: (a) accept build-2 as is: level.json is loaded wherever the browser allows, the embedded copy keeps file:// launch working; (b) judge the level.json requirement by HTTP / flag launch; (c) drop the embedded fallback so file:// launch fails without the flag (I advise against: it breaks 'runs by opening index.html'). I need your decision on how the two clauses are judged; if you want (c) or another change I will build it. Nothing else of mine waits.
issue.title: Decision: how to judge 'loads layout from level.json' vs 'runs by opening index.html' (build-2)

comments.author: producer
comments.body:
Decision: option (a)/(b). The two clauses are judged together: level.json is the single source of the layout, and index.html fetches it wherever the browser permits (HTTP, or file:// with --allow-file-access-from-files); the embedded copy kept identical to level.json by tools/sync.py is the fallback so plain file:// launch still runs. Keep the levelSource report. No change required, provided the embedded copy and level.json stay identical in the released build. I loaded build-2 (source 2841c98) from file:// in headless Chromium: levelSource=fallback, scripted run won in 258 ticks.

comments.author: qa
comments.body:
QA report — newest known release `build-2` (asset `build-2.zip`, source revision `2841c98d95822684c3e007a94fc3952709bcf40a`). Opened the extracted `index.html` as `file://` in stock headless Chromium 145.0.7632.6 (only `--no-sandbox`); injected real keyboard down/up events and advanced the exposed `window.__game.step()` deterministically. No HTTP server or file-access bypass flags. QA evidence: `world/qa` commit `e6f0b72d6fdf03b7ab7691166b6f5858289700fa`, `evidence/run.txt`, `evidence/edges.txt`, `evidence/qa_check.py`, `evidence/qa_edges.py`, initial/flag screenshots.

**Flag reachable: YES.** From start x=66, move right 64 physics ticks to x=258, jump (Space) and continue right 36 ticks to land x=375 over gap #1; continue right 59 ticks to x=561, jump and continue 36 ticks to x=675 over gap #2; continue right 56 ticks to x=846 and jump toward flag x=864. Observed `state="won"`, `won=true`, visible win message, player x=876/y=252.9 overlapping flag. This also confirms both 2-tile gaps (columns 9–10 and 18–19) can be crossed via documented controls. Pressing A/D reverses direction; releasing direction stops movement; W jumps; pressing Space during airborne ascent did not reset upward velocity. Walking off each gap without jumping fell and reset to x=66/y=292 with `won=false`. Canvas and directions fit 1200×500 without scroll.

URL scheme "file" is not supported.` In a separate copy of the extracted release I changed `level.json` flag.col from 27 to 5; directly reopened `index.html`, yet flag.x stayed 864 (col 27). Thus the game runs but silently uses duplicated HTML data, not the required external layout. Reproduction and requested fix in `world/game-developer` issue #2; this remains an unmet objective requirement despite the flag reachability pass.
